reviewer: Claude Code with sole fresh-context medium reviewer

claims.summary: For X={1..n}, Y=X+h on the line (h=floor(sqrt n), n>=4), nested graphs G_k={|x-y|<=e^(k-1)} for k from any k_0<=1 (or all integers) up to complete, weights w_k=e^k and m_k the deficiency of G_k: sum_k w_k m_k <= e^2 h^2/(e-1)+e h/(e-1) while every perfect matching M has sum_k w_k |M minus G_k| >= n(h-1). So per-level Hall deficiencies cannot be glued into one matching at any constant factor.
claims.assessment: Working elementary proof (counterexample proposed by the review's medium reviewer, checked and stated for levels of every radius): deficiencies by Hall's condition on X and explicit shifts, edge cost at least its length beyond length 1, and sum(y-x)=nh for every perfect matching.
claims.rationale: Refutes the per-level-deficiency form of the first route review's alternative architecture: per-level counts do not control displacement lengths, so a correct per-level bound integrates over level sets of one potential, the class formulation.
claims.next_action: None for the gluing step; a per-level condition with completion lengths remains queued.

claims.summary: Simulation, N=16*4^J uniform points, J=6..10, eight seeds each: the dyadic flow plus a greedy circulation per square (curl of a pyramid, chosen to minimize the quartic cost of the running field) has per-point kurtosis, after division by the dyadic flow's analytic per-position standard deviation, 2.71-2.89 against 2.88-3.19 for the dyadic flow, lower at every size with no trend in J, and moves variance from the first coordinate to the second (mean ratios 0.70-0.76 and 1.16-1.24).
claims.assessment: Finite check, two runs with expectations committed before each; the second fixes a diagonal-tie defect of the first. Controls: flux and global average pass; the per-level variance control failed as stated in 5 of 320 values, all at level 4 (sampling error; mean ratios 0.99-1.02); the reference predictions partly failed (raw mixture kurtosis formula off by up to 0.30, three of ten per-position slopes outside their band). The test is not decided: no growing gap at reachable sizes.
claims.rationale: The first route review's decisive test of the one adaptive mechanism the obstacle leaves open.
claims.next_action: Try adaptive choices acting on fluxes at scales coarser than one parent square, or the tube flow of a matching.

relationships: The reference flow; tests whether an adaptive correction escapes its Gaussian per-point tails.
Shows the per-level alternative to the class formulation fails; the class supremum is retained.
